_comment: Which local tests run on GitHub Actions, and in which order they are turned on.  Enabling more is a reviewed edit of this file.
The single workflow .github/workflows/ci.yml compiles once per platform ('build' job), uploads the workspace, then runs every
(platform, job) pair that has an enabled entry as its own 'test' job (in parallel, each on a fresh machine, so jobs cannot interfere through

ports, config directories or temp files; the lanes of one job - see 'job' below - and the entries of one lane run one after another on that machine). Test assemblies are prebuilt; some integration journeys restore temporary fixture projects using the populated package cache.
throughBatch: entries whose batch is greater than this are planned but not run.  workflow_dispatch can override it.

focus: true runs only the 'observe' entries on each platform (a 'required' one has passed twice in a row), which saves runner time while many entries still fail; a lane left with no entry is not scheduled.  workflow_dispatch with full=true runs everything once; set focus to false to return to full runs.
Per platform an entry is 'observe' (runs; a failure is reported as a warning and does not fail the job), 'required' (a failure fails
the job) or 'excluded' (does not run; 'reason' says why).  A platform missing from an entry is excluded.  A new batch starts as 'observe';
promote it to 'required' after it has been green on that platform for several runs.

A device journey (a real Android emulator or an iOS Simulator) may run only in a lane that declares its class under 'deviceClasses' together with the OS family whose runner hosts the device: 'macos' for the iOS Simulator, which is a native macOS process, and 'linux' for the Android emulator, which needs KVM. .github/ci/tests/verify-no-device-journeys.ps1 fails the plan job for any entry that runs a device class from a lane that does not declare it, and for a declared lane whose runner is not of that family. Every other entry stays off devices; those journeys run by hand on a developer machine.
An entry may carry 'env' (name -> value): those variables are set for that entry's test process only (run-test-plan.ps1), which is how one entry pins OD_WINUI_RUNTIME without affecting the next.
kind: xunit-exe = dotnet <target> [args] (an xUnit v3 test assembly, run directly); msbuild = dotnet msbuild <target> -t:Build.
'project' is built once in the build job (distinct projects only).  'measuredSeconds' is the last measured duration; keep it current when promoting a batch.

'buildFirst' projects are built before everything else on every platform that builds: the host's build writes the host-assembly manifest that lets every add-in trim what the host already ships (without it each add-in carries ~550 MB of copy-local dependencies and AddIns reaches 13 GB); tests/OpenDevelop.IntegrationTests/TESTING.md says the same: build the application first.

'buildArgs' are extra dotnet build arguments for the entry's 'project'; entries that share a project must agree on them.  The integration project is built with -p:BuildIntegrationFixtures=false because its fixture target builds every fixture inside one MSBuild process (Uno.Sdk 6.6.42 then clashes with the already resolved 6.5.31, MSB4240); a lane that needs a fixture lists that fixture's own csproj as an entry 'project' so it builds in its own process.

A lane with 'needsNuGetCache' also downloads the build job's NuGet package cache: the IDE host resolves its LibreWPF assemblies from the global packages folder at run time, so a lane that starts the IDE (the integration lanes) needs it; the unit lane does not.

'buildLast' projects are built after everything else, with their own 'args' ('{rid}' is the platform's 'rid').  The host is built last with '--runtime <rid> -p:AppendRuntimeIdentifierToOutputPath=false', the recipe terminal-cross-platform.yml uses (it builds the Terminal add-in that way, which builds the host project it references as that RID into the same folder) and whose IDE does start on the Windows runner.  Measured on the runner without it: the host's OpenDevelop.deps.json is 166 libraries without a 'PresentationFramework/11.0.0.0' reference entry from the very first host build on, whatever is built afterwards in the default way (a macOS build has 193, with 28 'reference' entries for the LibreWPF assemblies), and the IDE dies at start-up with a FileNotFoundException for PresentationFramework 11.0.0.0.  The build summary records the host deps.json after every build, so the run shows what the RID-specific build changes.

A lane definition holds 'timeoutMinutes', optionally 'needsNuGetCache' (the IDE host resolves its LibreWPF assemblies from the global packages folder at run time), 'needsGtk' for native GTK dependencies, and 'entryTimeoutMinutes' (an entry's default budget), and 'job': lanes of one platform that name the same job run one after another in ONE CI job, so the platform's archive is downloaded and unpacked once (the quick lanes - unit, integration-stable, integration-unstable - are job 'fast'; the long designer lane is its own job and runs in parallel); a job's timeout is the sum of its lanes' timeouts plus 30 minutes of preparation headroom.  A lane may also name 'runner' (its job runs on that image instead of the platform's, which is how the iOS Simulator lane gets Xcode 27) and 'deviceClasses' (the device journeys it may run, with the OS family that hosts the device - see the entry above). A platform may also name 'singleJob' to run all of its lanes in one job; no platform does now (macOS did, and its merged job exceeded the job timeout). A lane that names 'standalone' stays out of that merge and keeps its own job: mobile-ios does, because the Simulator lane needs the xcode-27 image, its SDK 11 and a booted simulator, which must not share the machine that runs the other macOS lanes.

'additionalProjects' declares fixture projects needed by an enabled entry; optional platforms refer to the build platform, so Windows ARM64 prerequisites belong to windows-x64 when it supplies the shared archive.

Profiler and Terminal are entries here; their own workflows (profiler.yml, terminal-cross-platform.yml) were deleted when they were folded in. Windows ARM64 and macOS ARM64 start as observed Terminal journeys and are promoted after repeated green runs.

platformNotes.macos-arm64: dist.macos.sh ships an osx-arm64-only payload, so this platform builds for itself and its archive drops the Windows RID trees the package never contains. It splits into 'fast' and 'designer' jobs like Windows and Linux, plus the standalone mobile-ios job. The merged single 'macos' job (commit 66e0c934ed) timed out, so it was split back.
platformNotes.windows-x64: Every unit and integration entry is required here since 2026-10-27 (base-tests and xamldom-tests-microsoftwpf were the last unit entries promoted), so a focus run executes only its observe entries here: a few in the fast job and the integration-winui and integration-winui-microsoft jobs, whose entries are all observe. Its build also supplies windows-arm64.
platformNotes.windows-arm64: Runs the native Windows ARM64 Terminal journey against the same unified Windows payload the x64 lane tests: dist.windows.bat ships one package with runtimes/ plus per-RID win-x64/win-arm64 folders and both launchers, so 'buildFrom': 'windows-x64' keeps a single compile for both lanes.
platformNotes.linux-x64: Enabled on 2026-11-02 with the unit suites (Profiler among them, which profiler.yml once ran on ubuntu-latest) and the workbench and DevFlow journeys, all 'observe'. The IDE entries run under xvfb-run with Mesa's software Vulkan driver (install-linux-prerequisites.sh); promote per the usual two green runs.
platformNotes.linux-arm64: Same entries and rules as linux-x64, on the native ubuntu-26.04-arm runner: dist.linux.sh ships one archive per Linux architecture, so each builds for itself.

unit.note: The unit suites, run like every other lane from the archive of their platform's build, first in its platform's 'fast' job; Windows ARM64 ('buildFrom': 'windows-x64') runs the x64 build it ships. An entry gets 10 minutes, so one that hangs (for example a test whose child application cannot open a window) cannot use up the whole lane; the longest measured entry took about a minute (base-tests 61-64 s, profiler-tests 43-44 s on the Linux unit jobs of run 41393644443), and the job timeout (the lanes' timeouts plus 30 minutes) leaves room for unpacking the archive and restoring the package cache.

integration-stable.note: Entries that passed on every hosted run in which the IDE started (runs 40431285339 through 40461019311): workbench, the stable core journeys, code coverage and the ARM64 unit suites, sharing one preparation. Windows x64 measured about 28 minutes of tests plus ~15 minutes of preparation. Its entries are required on macOS ARM64 and Windows x64 after each passed on the last two hosted runs that completed it there; on Windows ARM64 they are required too, after passing on runs 40444468212, 40461019311 and 40470967407. In focus mode the lane has no entry left and is not scheduled. new-project-dialog-macos joined later: it failed on the hosted runner until cc569fd5a8 and moved here after passing runs 40606824351 and 40615707034.

integration-designer.note: All designer journeys (LibreWPF, LibreWinForms, MewUI, GTK) in one lane. Entries in a lane run serially, so the LibreWPF journeys that edit src/Samples still never share the sample with a concurrent test. Windows: ~15 minutes preparation, 3.5 minutes GTK install, 24-28 minutes of LibreWPF editing. macOS runs it as its own 'designer' job, like Windows and Linux.

mobile-ios.note: The iOS Simulator debugging journey (Debugger.AddIn's IosSimulatorProjectBehavior) on the xcode-27 image: an iOS Simulator is a native macOS process, so no nested virtualisation is involved. The image has Xcode 27.2 at /Applications/Xcode_27.2.app and an iOS 27.2 simulator; CI selects that stable toolchain and installs the current .NET 11 iOS workload that requires it. The journey registers that SDK through od.sdk.add-custom-root and attaches SharpDbg to the app it installs with simctl. The lane is 'standalone', so it keeps its own job on xcode-27 and the other macOS lanes never install the workload or boot a simulator. allowAllFailures is the bootstrap exception (a lane whose only entry failed fails the lane): drop it and promote the entry to required after two green runs.

mobile-android.note: The Android debugging journey (Debugger.AddIn's AndroidDebugProjectBehavior) against a headless emulator on the hosted ubuntu-latest runner, the only runner image family with KVM (macOS arm64 and ubuntu-26.04-arm have no nested virtualisation). The job enables /dev/kvm, installs the android workload next to the SDK 11 it puts in ~/.dotnet, and boots one google_apis x86_64 AVD, whose ABI the archive's AddIns/Debugger/android/x86_64 agent covers. allowAllFailures is the bootstrap exception (a lane whose only entry failed fails the lane): drop it and promote the entry to required after two green runs. A runner whose host exposes no usable /dev/kvm skips the emulator and this lane with a warning instead of failing the job.

integration-unstable.note: Entries with known hosted failures or under investigation: macOS Terminal pointer input and debugger-journeys on Windows ARM64 (one flaky stop, fixed in c7497292df, awaiting a second green run). base-tests-arm, add-reference-journey and debugger-feature-journeys are required on every platform since 2026-10-28 but stay here for now: moving them into integration-stable would lengthen a lane with a 55-minute timeout that nobody has re-measured, and a full run is not due yet. Plan order runs the required entries first, then Hot Reload; keep any entry that can hang for tens of minutes after the required ones. The WinUI observe entries moved to the integration-winui and integration-winui-microsoft lanes. It is the last lane of the shared fast job, so its pointer journeys run after the other lanes of that job: a leftover IDE window from an observe entry must not sit in front of a designer drag.

integration-winui.note: Surface, host selection and Uno (entries winui-surface-designer-journeys, winui-host-selection, winui-uno-cell), split out of the former single winui job (the rest is integration-winui-microsoft) so the two jobs run in parallel with about equal length (measured run 44308680459: 427+191+778 s here against 299+393+225+121+663 s there, each plus about 12 minutes of preparation). Surface runs first: a leftover IDE window must not sit in front of its real-pointer drag. The job timeout is the lane budget plus 30 minutes of headroom, and that headroom also has to hold about 12 minutes of preparation and the best-effort Visual Studio MSBuild host build (bounded to 25 minutes); the entries measured about 23 minutes in total. The entry budgets sum to 105 minutes, so the lane budget of 120 is never the limit; the risk is the job timeout of 150: up to 21 minutes of preparation plus the 25-minute host build plus 105 minutes of entries is 151, which would cancel the job and lose its summary. Reaching it needs every entry to run to its own budget, which is far from the measured 23 minutes (accepted risk). Windows x64 only; observe, allowAllFailures because the runner may lack the Windows App Runtime or the interactive desktop; promote after two green runner runs.

integration-winui-microsoft.note: The Microsoft WinUI cell and the real WinUI-Gallery and WPF-Gallery corpora (the other half of the former single winui job; see integration-winui) in a job of their own, so their long first renders and Windows App SDK prerequisites cannot stretch the fast job. ci.yml clones the Gallery for this job. Windows x64 only; every entry starts as observe. allowAllFailures because the runner may lack Visual Studio MSBuild or the Windows App SDK, which fails every entry at once; promote entries, and drop this flag, after two green runner runs. The job also runs a best-effort Visual Studio MSBuild step that builds the Microsoft design hosts before the lane (bounded to 25 minutes, not yet measured); the job timeout is the lane budget plus 30 minutes of preparation headroom, so if that build plus the usual 11-15 minutes of archive preparation exceeds the headroom, raise the lane timeoutMinutes after the first runner run.

buildLast.note: macOS and Linux are single-architecture payloads (dist.macos.sh, dist.linux.sh), so building the add-in for that RID is harmless and stages the native Terminal assets the lanes use. On Windows the unified payload already carries runtimes/win-x64 and win-arm64, so a RID build is what used to strip the host folder - the build guard rejects it there.
Publish the Windows host after the RID-specific Terminal build restores its mutable payload outputs.

Opens the shared Device Manager, reads the same snapshot, refreshes every provider and closes it. Contents are platform-dependent (the host row always exists), so only the snapshot shape is asserted. Starts as observe.

The AddIn Manager Installed list in an isolated IDE: shipped add-ins are preinstalled without Uninstall, a user-directory add-in stays uninstallable. Was written with the preinstalled classification but had no CI entry. Starts as observe.
Trust, install and update an add-in against a fake GitHub release feed in an isolated IDE. Self-contained (no network); it existed without a CI entry. Starts as observe.

The empty-startup journey (Start Page add-in loaded, Start Page is the active view). It shares WorkbenchTests.cs with the workbench-tests entry, whose -class filter does not select it, so it never ran in CI. It needs a fresh application, hence its own entry. Starts as observe.

The Debug toolbar launch-target drop-down on a multi-target project: profiles from launchSettings.json, hidden frameworks, adding a profile, choosing a device. It only reads the device list (a simulator is stored by UDID when the machine has one); it never boots or installs anything. Had no CI entry. Starts as observe.

Regression gates behind the fast-mode work: an idle window and an idle IDE after an ILSpy search stay under a share of one core, and a second build of an unchanged solution skips every project (changed, added and referenced-project changes are rebuilt). The idle thresholds are CPU ratios, not wall-clock times, but a loaded shared runner can still move them, so this stays observe until it has been green on each platform. Had no CI entry.

Each of SDK 10 and SDK 11 selected before startup, via a root that holds only that SDK: the project loads with items and builds. Nothing is downloaded. Skips a major the machine has no stable SDK for. macOS ARM64: 2 passed in 67 seconds. Starts as observe.
net11.0 projects: build fails with NETSDK1045 under an SDK 10 only root, and builds, runs and debugs under an SDK 11 only root. macOS ARM64: 3 passed in 76 seconds. Starts as observe.

A net10.0 project builds and debugs, and after its project file is retargeted to net11.0 it builds and debugs again. Skips itself where no .NET 11 runtime is installed. Only .NET 10 and 11 are covered; older runtimes are not tested. Starts as observe.

Issue #24: the real Project Browser context menu on a project node (Rename, Delete, Remove present and enabled), then rename and delete on a copy of SlnxFixture - the .csproj, the .slnx entry and a rebuild under the new name. Starts as observe.

One fact checks the exit code and the log; the other finds the WPF dialog through EnumWindows, posts WM_CLOSE and requires the same exit, which is why it runs on Windows only. It passes on hosted macOS ARM64 and Windows x64; on Windows ARM64 the dialog never got native focus because the image sits on the first-logon privacy page; the Prepare the Windows desktop step (32fd2eda79) clears it, and it then passed runs 40662664664 and 40671568295 there.

The trait selection is accepted by tests/verify-no-device-journeys.ps1 only on Windows entries (the device journeys sharing AddInTests skip themselves there). The Surface is the default WinUI selection, so no OD_WINUI_RUNTIME pin is needed. It sits in integration-winui (allowAllFailures) because the runner may lack the prerequisites that would make this entry fail while it is observe: the Windows App Runtime (windowsappruntimeinstall-x64.exe --quiet --force), a .NET SDK the provisioner can build the matched host with, and the interactive desktop that prepare-windows-desktop.ps1 sets up for the real-pointer journeys. The first open provisions a matched host (about a minute cold). run-test-plan.ps1 fails the entry if every test skipped (a missing Surface payload). Starts as observe; promote after two green runner runs.

entries.note: The real WPFGallery application of microsoft/WPF-Samples against the Microsoft WPF design host (WpfGalleryDesignerTests, the WPF counterpart of the WinUI Gallery corpus; its opt-in full sweep stays off). ci.yml sparse-clones Sample Applications/WPFGallery of WPF-Samples into the runner temp folder and exports OD_WPF_GALLERY_ROOT; OD_WPF_GALLERY_BUILD=1 makes the class build the Gallery through DevFlow before the first page opens (an unbuilt checkout renders pages without their sample controls). Needs the Microsoft WPF design host (MicrosoftWpfDesign.SurfaceHost), which the plan's build job does not produce: the best-effort step Build the Microsoft designer hosts of the winui and winui-microsoft jobs runs the integration project's BuildMicrosoftDesignerHostsForIntegrationTests target (build.ps1 with Visual Studio MSBuild for the WPF, WinUI and WinForms hosts and the WinUI sample), and without that host every case fails at first render (WPF designer never finished loading). It sits in integration-winui-microsoft only to share that job's archive preparation. READ THE ENTRY'S ROW: the clone step is best-effort, so a failed clone skips every case, which run-test-plan.ps1 records as failed (every test skipped). Starts as observe; promote after two green runner runs.

entries.reason: The Microsoft WinUI host and the Windows App SDK Gallery are Windows-only; ARM64 has not been measured.
entries.note: The four single-page Gallery cases (routing, settings page, visual states). Split out of the former winui-gallery-corpus entry, whose single 90-minute budget let a host that never starts burn 150 s on each of 24 pages.
